newsitem.title: UK: UK supermarkets withdraw cornflakes in nut scare.
newsitem.headline: UK supermarkets withdraw cornflakes in nut scare.

text.p: Three British supermarket chains withdrew thousands of packets of cornflakes on Friday because they might contain nuts that could trigger a potentially fatal allergy.

Some of the plain cornflake packets provided by the same supplier were believed to contain some honeynut cornflakes, so Somerfield, Sainsbury's and Happy Shopper Cornflakes, which are sold at 40,000 independent outlets, took them off the market.
An allergy to nuts, triggering anaphylactic shock, is thought to affect up to one in 100 people in Britain and causes about five deaths a year.
"We think statistically the likelihood of anybody having a problem is incredibly small but I'm afraid one is one too many," a Somerfield spokeswoman told BBC Television.
